clinical_course: Visual field loss without antecedent symptoms. Symptoms improved as the cabin passed 15,000 ft on descent and resolved by landing-pattern altitude. Contemporary interpretation was probable hypoglycemia.
The pilot remained asymptomatic during the fitting and reported a scintillating left scotoma shortly after leaving the chamber. The symptom resolved approximately 30 minutes after onset.

Generalized joint pain developed on an aircraft flight at a cabin altitude above 40,000 ft. The pain gradually resolved on descent. The summary describes one of the four closely spaced dysbarism episodes without neurologic symptoms.
Left peripheral visual loss developed without preceding joint pain. It cleared below 20,000 ft. Abdominal-wall symptoms occurred during a subsequent leg of the same flight.
Central visual loss cleared on descent to 15,000 ft.
Joint pain and left arm and neck numbness preceded abdominal-wall swelling and confusion. Symptoms improved on descent. The flight surgeon diagnosed presumptive dysbarism with CNS involvement.

Elbow pain and abdominal-wall symptoms preceded a left peripheral scotoma. The visual symptom persisted approximately 90 minutes and cleared on descent to 15,000 ft. The report describes headache and fatigue during hospitalization.
Right flank burning and epigastric pain preceded left homonymous hemianopia. Symptoms initially remained after descent. The examiner considered DCS alongside a conversion reaction.
The pilot was told 30,000 ft. The chamber never exceeded 12,000 ft. The report explicitly describes four hours without symptoms.

clinical_course: Shoulder numbness preceded dizziness and left peripheral scotoma. The scotoma persisted for about ten minutes at ground pressure. Oxygen toxicity was considered at the time before the clinical assessment of recurrent DCS.

Early pruritus preceded abdominal mottling, numbness and perimetrically mapped right homonymous scotoma. Cognitive impairment was observed during plotting. The role of the oxygen and carbon dioxide mixture given before descent remained undetermined.

clinical_course: Reported deltoid numbness and tender cutaneous lesion were followed by mottling and presyncope. Initial scratching preceded the first reported symptom. Examination found no objective neurologic deficit or visual field change. Descent followed the 122-minute finding.
